Heard on I.A. No.4833/2023, first application under Section 389 (1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of the appellant - Karu @
Mukesh Shakya.

This criminal appeal assails the judgment dated 05.07.2022 passed in Special Case No.15/2020 by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Lahar, District Bhind (M.P.),
whereby the appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:-

sentences.text: In brief, case of the prosecution is that on 05.07.2017 mother of prosecutrix with her father-in-law lodged a report at Police Station Aswar District Bhind to the effect that on 03.07.2017 at about 7:30 am, her daughter (Prosecutrix) had gone to the field to attend the call of nature and did not come back.
When father-in-law of the complainant searched the prosecutrix, he came to know that the appellant has eloped the prosecutrix on the pretext of marriage.
On his information, FIR bearing crime No.27/2017 for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366 of IPC was registered against the appellant.
On 07.07.2017, prosecutrix was recovered.
She was sent for medical examination.

Appellant was arrested and after completion of investigation Karu @ Mukesh Shakya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34693931/

sentences.text: , charge-sheet was submitted.
After conclusion of trial, trial Court convicted and sentenced the appellant for the offence as mentioned above.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated in this case and the trial Court has committed an error in convicting and sentencing the appellant.
It is further submitted that in the statements of prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., prosecutrix has not alleged against the present applicant for commission of rape.
Appellant was on bail during trial and he did not misuse the liberty so granted to him.
Appellant has suffered about five years and three months of jail incarceration and he is the permanent resident of District- Bhind (M.P.).
There are fair chances of success of this appeal.
Final hearing of the appeal will take some time.
Under these circumstances, the execution of jail sentence be suspended and the appellant be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent/State opposed the bail application and prayed for rejection of this application.
Keeping in view of the aforesaid submissions of learned counsel for the parties but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, IA No.4833/2023 is allowed.

It is, therefore, directed that if appellant deposits the entire fine amount, if not already deposited, and furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 6th December, 2023 and on such subsequent dates as may be fixed in this regard,
sentence of imprisonment awarded to him, shall remain suspended till further orders and he shall be released on bail.
The appellant shall mark his presence before concerned Police Station once in every fortnight.
IA No.4833/2023 stands allowed and disposed of.
